The official generator first makes windows of at most L items, using backward sliding starts plus start zero. Each window receives d=dupe_factor random reconstruction copies **plus one additional terminal-only masked copy**; these share the original window but are shuffled together, without paired batching or paired loss. Random reconstruction selects shuffled eligible positions without replacement, targeting min(max_predictions_per_seq, max(1, round(window_length × masked_lm_prob))). Selected positions retain their original labels; mask_prob controls replacement, with its remaining probability split equally between unchanged and random items. Separately, force_last=True evaluation keeps only the final L items and masks the last eligible item. Thus truncation includes the target within L positions; terminal masking replaces it rather than appending another position. [Official generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py)

The supplied MovieLens script uses d=10 and mask_prob=1.0, so every selected reconstruction position becomes [MASK]. [Official configuration](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run_ml-1m.sh) Training sums full-vocabulary cross-entropy across all active targets in a minibatch and divides by their total weight plus 1e-5; padded targets have zero weight. It does not first average each sequence’s loss. [Official loss](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py)

Consequently, Bernoulli terminal allocation is a sampling approximation, not the reference generation procedure: p=1/(d+1) matches the terminal-only example proportion only in expectation, without guaranteeing d reconstruction copies and one terminal copy per window. Random copies can also select terminal positions. Loss normalization matters: if reconstruction examples contain k targets, the dedicated terminal copies contribute roughly 1/(dk+1) of target weight, rather than 1/(d+1). These are attribution details; the supplied host baseline, fixed splits and left-padding contract remain authoritative.
